title: Maryland AI Laws

reading.body:
Maryland has enacted three AI-related laws, all passed on May 12, 2026, covering election deepfakes, identity fraud via AI, and a statewide 3-1-1 chatbot program.

The three laws split into two directions. SB141 and SB8 create criminal and civil liability for deceptive uses of AI, specifically election-related deepfakes and identity fraud using AI or deepfake representations. SB114 instead mandates deployment of AI chatbots and voicebots in the state's 3-1-1 system, with multilingual support, GIS integration, and escalation protocols.

For AI, this means Maryland is simultaneously restricting harmful synthetic media and requiring government use of conversational AI. The laws do not address compute, data centers, or power. The data also does not include effective dates, penalty amounts, or enforcement resources, so it cannot show how quickly or firmly these rules will take hold.

Maryland has enacted 3 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Maryland

3 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • SB141: Election Law - Election Misinformation, Election Disinformation, and Deepfakes passed 2026-05-12

    Requires the State Administrator of Elections to correct election misinformation and disinformation, authorizes injunctions and subpoenas, allows the State Board of Elections to sue for damages, and makes it a misdemeanor to knowingly or recklessly create, use, or disseminate certain election-related deepfakes.

  • SB8: Criminal Law - Identity Fraud - Artificial Intelligence and Deepfake Representations passed 2026-05-12

    Amends Maryland's identity fraud statute to prohibit using personal identifying information without consent to cause harm, and to prohibit using artificial intelligence or deepfake representations to impersonate, falsely depict, or claim to represent another person with fraudulent intent, or to create or distribute false records to cause harm, induce disclosure of personal identifying information, or obtain a benefit. It establishes criminal penalties and a private civil action for victims of AI or deepfake violations.

  • SB114: 3-1-1 Systems - Expansion Program and Oversight Board - Establishment passed 2026-05-12

    Establishes the Maryland 3-1-1 Oversight Board within the Maryland Information Network and a 3-1-1 Program to evaluate and expand 3-1-1 systems. Requires the Board to designate counties, select vendors, and deploy AI chatbots and voicebots with multilingual support, GIS integration, and escalation protocols. Requires statewide implementation by July 1, 2028 and reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Maryland. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
